messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel 6.3.12 bump in us-west2 last night, we saw transient Xid bursts on gfx1/gfx2/gfx5. DCGM exporter fired a big flurry of Xid/ECC alerts and oncall got a wall of pages.

 tim: saw that. clusterscale: a lot of the alerts were single-event spikes that cleared quickly. We need to avoid mass-drains from noisy cards.

 sasha: Agree. Proposal: coalesce Xid spikes per PCI slot into a rolling 'streak' metric and only escalate after N consecutive 5m windows exceed a per-card delta. Also add cluster-wide throttle so we don't evict >2% of nodes at once.

 maria: Sketch of heuristics I used during triage:
- record Xid increase per-device with increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])
- device_streak = count_over_time(increase(...) > 0)[20m]  # how many 5m windows had events
- mark_flaky if device_streak >= 3
- only trigger drain/evict if mark_flaky persists for 3 consecutive 20m checks AND cluster_flaky_fraction < 0.02

 jun: can you paste a Prom rule snippet? we can try in staging.

 sasha:
```
# recording rule: per-device xid delta over 5m
- record: xid:increase:5m
  expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])

# alert rule: per-device flaky window
- alert: GPUDeviceFlakyWindow
  expr: xid:increase:5m > 0
  for: 0s
  labels:
    severity: warning

# higher-level alert: device marked flaky after repeating windows (when run through a recording rule pipeline)
- alert: GPUDeviceMarkedFlaky
  expr: (sum_over_time((xid:increase:5m > 0)[20m:5m]) >= 3)
  for: 0s
  labels:
    severity: critical
```

 maria: The important bit is we don't use immediate hard drains. For remediation we fallback to cordon+background-evict where evictions are rate-limited by a cluster metric `cluster_eviction_rate{job="ops"}`.

 devops: add a small hysteresis: when we cordon, don't auto-replace until we observe a kernel oops or consecutive ECC increases across reboots. Otherwise we waste RMA cycles.

 tim: Also recommend adding a suppression window for driver-upgrade times to reduce false positives: set silence annotation for nodes with `driver_upgrade=true` tag for 30m.

 oncall-bot: FYI — created incident 2026-09-14-uw2-xid-spike, linked runbook: https://runbooks.internal/r/uw2-xid

 jun: Plan to test in staging tonight. Steps:
1) add recording rule file to staging-prometheus: `/etc/prometheus/rules/xid-streaks.yaml`
2) `kubectl apply -f /ops/prometheus/staging/xid-streaks.yaml`
3) run synthetic DCGM injector: `./tools/fake-xid --card=gfx2 --burst=3 --interval=60s`
4) validate that alerts escalate only after 3 windows

 maria: ok. I'll push a WIP PR with the rule and a short note about cluster_eviction caps. tagging @sasha @tim for review :eyes:

 sasha: thanks — if staging looks good we can roll to prod with a 1-hour ramp and emergency rollback to previous prom rules.

 tim: can we add metrics to Console dashboard: per-node `xid:increase:5m` and `device_streak` so SREs can see progression before alerts fire?

 maria: Yep I'll add panel and a simple log query for `journalctl -u nvidia-node` to surface driver messages in the console panel.

 devops: +1. Also let's ensure the alert notification includes node labels (sku, rack) so support doesn't page wrong team.

 oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled kernel rollout window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC; consider muting or applying the suppression rule during the window :calendar:

 maria: noted. Will include suppression in the rollout checklist.

 sasha: great work triaging. small follow-up: add a separate rule for `dcgm_ecc_corrected_errors_total` — large spikes there may still require RMA even if Xid is noisy.

 maria: adding to PR. closing thread after staging test — will update here.
